Architecture Diagram

PhotoGallery is a single ASP.NET MVC web application that presents photos stored in Azure Blob Storage. Browsers retrieve the gallery page from the application and load public blob URLs directly from the storage service.

Data Storage & External Services

The application stores image objects in one Azure Blob Storage container and has no relational database, cache, or message broker. The controller lists and mutates blobs; the browser receives blob URIs and loads them directly. The container is created with blob-level public read access.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • A single MVC controller coordinates the UI and Azure Blob Storage operations; no separate service or repository layer is present.
  • Blob data is exposed through direct storage URLs rather than proxied through the web application.
  • Listing and deletion use synchronous SDK operations while create/upload/delete operations are asynchronous in some actions.

DTOs & Contracts

No dedicated request/response DTOs or immutable contract classes are present. The gallery view receives List; upload uses ASP.NET Request.Files; delete accepts a string form value. BlobItem and BlobClient are Azure SDK types, not application-owned API DTOs. No OpenAPI, protobuf, or GraphQL contract is present. Package declarations include Newtonsoft.Json and System.Text.Json, but no application serialization configuration was found.

Communication Patterns

The browser communicates with the MVC application over HTTP. The controller makes direct calls to Azure Blob Storage: listing operations use synchronous SDK calls, while container creation, uploads, and deletes use asynchronous calls in some actions. No queues, events, retries, circuit breakers, service discovery, load balancing, or API gateway are configured. The application stores a static BlobContainerClient and initializes it in the gallery action.

No authentication, authorization, or application-level TLS configuration was identified. The container is created with blob-level public read access; storage URLs are returned to browsers. IIS Express is configured for local HTTP on port 20050; production transport settings are not included.

Core Business Workflows

PhotoGallery is a photo gallery that lets a user view images stored in a cloud blob container, upload images, and remove one or all stored images. The application exposes a single gallery workflow backed by Azure Blob Storage.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
PhotoBlobPhoto GalleryAn image object displayed by the galleryStored in one BlobContainer
BlobContainerPhoto StorageCollection that contains gallery image objectsContains many PhotoBlob objects

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
WebApp-Storage-DotNetGallery presentation and photo managementNo independent database-owned entities; coordinates PhotoBlob operationsAzure Blob Storage
Azure Blob StoragePhoto persistenceBlobContainer and PhotoBlob objectsNone identified

The storage service is the source of truth for photo data. The application retrieves blob URIs and the browser loads public photo content directly from storage; no inter-service exchange is present.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: View the Gallery

  1. The browser requests the gallery page.
  2. HomeController.Index constructs a storage client, obtains the configured container, and ensures the container exists with blob-level public read access.
  3. The application enumerates block blobs and passes their URIs to the Razor view.
  4. The browser renders thumbnails and loads image content using the blob URLs.

Workflow 2: Upload Photos

  1. The user selects one or more files and posts a multipart request.
  2. HomeController.UploadAsync checks that the request has at least one file and generates a new blob name from the current tick count, a GUID, and the original file extension.
  3. The controller uploads each file and redirects to the gallery. The implementation passes the submitted FileName to the SDK's path-based upload overload.
  4. Storage failures return the error view. No file type, size, or per-request file-count validation is implemented in the controller.

Workflow 3: Delete Photos

The individual-delete action extracts a filename from the submitted URI and deletes that blob if it exists. The bulk-delete action enumerates the container and deletes block blobs. Both actions redirect to the gallery on success and return the error view on exceptions.

Cross-Service Data Flows

There is no multi-service aggregation. The application asks Azure Blob Storage for blob metadata and URIs, renders them in the gallery, and allows the browser to retrieve public blob content directly. Upload and delete requests are synchronous user workflows that invoke storage SDK operations; no fallback or offline store is configured.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant User as "Gallery User" participant App as "Photo Gallery" participant Storage as "Azure Blob Storage" User->>App: Request gallery App->>Storage: Ensure container and list block blobs Storage-->>App: Blob metadata and URIs App-->>User: Render gallery page User->>App: Submit selected files App->>App: Check file count and create blob names App->>Storage: Upload using submitted file path alt Upload succeeds Storage-->>App: Upload completed App-->>User: Redirect to gallery else Upload fails Storage-->>App: Storage exception App-->>User: Display error view end

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • The upload action proceeds only when the submitted file count is greater than zero; no additional type, size, or request-count rules are enforced in the controller.
  • New blob names combine a timestamp, a random GUID, and the original extension.
  • Individual deletion targets the last path segment of the submitted URI; bulk deletion handles block blobs only.
  • There is no explicit authentication, role check, ownership rule, or audit trail for gallery operations.
  • Storage exceptions are sent to the error view with exception details and stack trace. No transaction, compensation, or retry policy is configured.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The application targets .NET Framework 4.8 and uses an older MVC 5 stack. Several packages are old, including jQuery 1.10.2, Bootstrap 3.0.0, Newtonsoft.Json 6.0.8, and Microsoft.Net.Compilers 1.0.0. AppCAT dependency analysis could not resolve the legacy project because Visual Studio WebApplication MSBuild targets are not installed in the Linux environment; dependency counts therefore reflect declared packages only.

Notable Observations

  • No database or ORM packages are declared; Azure Blob Storage is the persistence service.
  • Both Newtonsoft.Json and System.Text.Json are declared, although no use of either was found in the application source.
  • UI libraries are checked into the project alongside NuGet declarations, and no lock file is present.

No application cache, cache provider, or cache-aside/read-through pattern is configured. Blob contents are fetched directly from Azure Storage.

Data Ownership Boundaries

The Azure container is the sole persistence store and the application's source of truth for photos. There is one deployable application and no cross-service database access, CQRS, or aggregation across services. The web tier obtains storage object URIs and the browser then reads blob content directly from the storage service.
